description: Long green stalks tied into a sheaf, damp from the ditch some blob had been squatting in.
lore: Nine people at one fire, nine names for it, every one of them certain. Marsh-tongue. Ditch-sorrel. Goosegrass, poor-man's-bay, the one the drovers call cutfinger, and a Latin one from a man who was a physician for thirty years and has not been one for four hundred. They agreed on exactly two things: boil it, and it is good with fish.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] wrote down all nine, which annoyed the entire fire, since eight of them are obviously wrong. She will not choose. Her position, stated once and never repeated, is that a plant nine people remember nine ways is a plant nine people are holding up, and [[lore/the_chronicle|the book]] is not in the business of taking eight of them away. The stall on that road sells it under the name everyone actually uses, which is bundle.
gm_notes: Bettany's editorial policy in miniature, argued over a weed. Useful whenever a player wants the Chronicle to settle a question of fact.
